summary.text: David McDonough of Merrick, was first elected to the Assembly in a special election on February 12, 2002, and represents the 14th Assembly District.
His official biography says he chairs the Assembly Minority Task Force on Public Safety and sits on the Transportation Committee.

paragraphs.text: McDonough's biography says he served in the U.S. Coast Guard and the U.S. Air Force, earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Columbia University and graduated from the American Academy of Dramatic Arts.
Before the Assembly he served four terms as president of the Merrick Chamber of Commerce, from 1994 to 1998, and is a past president of the Nassau County Council of Chambers of Commerce.
He helped coordinate the Merrick Downtown Revitalization Project and was a founding member of the Bellmore-Merrick Community Wellness Council.

In the Assembly he is an associate board member of the New York chapter of InfraGard, an FBI public-private partnership, and a member of the Nassau County Task Force on Family Violence, the biography says.
He has belonged to the Kiwanis Club of Merrick for more than 30 years, and he and his wife, Carolyn, live in Merrick and have three children and four grandchildren.
